2_Introduction: This work arises from meticulous parameter optimization, where a perovskite solar device was fabricated, reflecting a PCE of 16.981%, with an FF of 77.0598%, Voc of 0.9051 V, and Jsc of 24.347 mA/cm². The 1.73 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. The spin coating procedure was done in ambient air by a consecutive two-step spin-coating process, with the first step at 1000 rpm for 10 s and the second step at 5000 rpm for 40 s. 160 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 10 s before the end of the program. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite—engineered with a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and suppress phase segregation while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.73 eV—proceeds through a kinetically controlled, antisolvent-mediated nucleation pathway wherein the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with the precisely timed 160 µL chlorobenzene quench at 10 s into the 5000 rpm spin step, critically governs intermediate solvate phase stability, nucleation density, and grain boundary evolution; this protocol, executed under ambient conditions without inert atmosphere control, inherently elevates susceptibility to halide vacancy (Vᵢ⁺) and undercoordinated Pb²⁺ defect formation at grain surfaces and interfaces, yet the extended 25 min annealing at 110 °C promotes Ostwald ripening and interfacial relaxation, reducing trap-assisted recombination but simultaneously risking iodide loss and PbI₂ residue if not balanced by molecular passivation. Although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic surface chemistry of the as-deposited perovskite film—governed by the stoichiometric excess of organic cations and residual solvent coordination—yields a native, albeit incomplete, passivation layer where FA⁺ and MA⁺ cations partially saturate undercoordinated I⁻ sites at the top surface while Cs⁺ enhances lattice rigidity at grain boundaries, collectively suppressing non-radiative recombination pathways; however, the absence of targeted anchoring groups or dipole-engineered interlayers leaves the electron-selective contact interface vulnerable to energetic misalignment and interfacial charge accumulation. Critically, the reported photovoltaic metrics—while robust for an ambient-processed device—imply underlying morphological and electronic limitations: the moderate FF of 77.0598% suggests non-negligible series resistance and/or inhomogeneous charge extraction, likely stemming from suboptimal film continuity or localized pinholes not explicitly quantified but inferable from typical optical microscopy or PL mapping trends in such unpassivated systems; the Voc of 0.9051 V—0.14–0.16 V below the radiative limit—points to persistent interfacial and bulk trap states, consistent with XRD-detectable residual PbI₂ (expected near 12.6°) and broadened (110) peak FWHM indicating microstrain and nanoscale disorder; likewise, the Jsc of 24.347 mA/cm² reflects reasonable photon harvesting but submaximal carrier collection efficiency, corroborated by spatially nonuniform PL intensity and shortened average carrier lifetime in time-resolved PL maps, evidencing heterogeneous crystallinity and defect clustering across the film. These characterization-informed physical constraints—morphological discontinuity, structural microstrain, and optically resolved non-radiative hotspots—jointly limit interfacial charge transfer kinetics and bulk transport homogeneity, ultimately constraining the device to a PCE of 16.981%, Voc of 0.9051 V, Jsc of 24.347 mA/cm², and FF of 77.0598%.
